turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi there, how are you feeling today?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm cooking just for myself now, after twenty years of cooking for a family. It feels a bit pointless.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's a big change, and it makes sense that it feels strange. Cooking for one can still be a nice thing to do for yourself.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Everything I make lasts for days though.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You could cook a full recipe and freeze single portions. Then you have homemade ready meals on tired evenings.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's sensible. What about things that don't freeze?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Try dishes that are naturally small, like an omelette, a quick pasta, or a piece of fish with some greens. Ten minutes and no leftovers.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I used to make fish for the kids every Friday. Maybe

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'll keep doing that, just smaller.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That sounds like a lovely way to keep the tradition. Treat yourself to a nice piece.
